title: Migrating Iceberg to Jackson 3
summary: Alex Dutra opened a discussion on moving Iceberg from Jackson 2 to Jackson 3. The main difficulty is iceberg-core, where Jackson types appear in the public API of the parser classes, JsonUtil and the REST HTTP layer; he first suggested Jackson 3 overloads with both versions coexisting. Steve Loughran argued against putting Jackson 3 in signatures and proposed an indirection layer that hides the JSON binding, deprecating the Jackson 2 APIs or moving them to a legacy module. In November Alex adopted that direction: Iceberg-owned shim types, compatibility tests and both Jackson versions shipped during a transition. JB Onofré agreed and proposed doing the shims first while still on Jackson 2, deprecating Jackson-typed APIs in 1.13, running existing parser tests against both backends, and providing thin adapter artifacts with a Jackson module for REST servers. Alex and JB agreed on this phasing, starting with one PR that adds the shim types and migrates one parser package.

positions.stance: Reduce Jackson 2 exposure first by making parser classes and JsonUtil package-private or deprecated, and keep overloads or an indirection only for the ObjectMapper extension points.
Do not expose Jackson 3 in public signatures; add an API that hides the JSON binding, deprecate the Jackson 2 APIs with a clear removal plan, and move to Jackson 3 internally.
Introduce Iceberg-owned shims over Jackson types in the serde and REST layers and ship both Jackson versions during a transition period.

Introduce the shims first as a pure refactor on Jackson 2, and keep core binding agnostic with separate thin Jackson 2 and Jackson 3 adapter artifacts because REST servers need a Jackson module for their own mapper.

outcome.note: Alex Dutra and JB Onofré agreed on a phased plan: shim types and API deprecation first on Jackson 2, then adapter artifacts for the REST layer, dual-backend tests, the switch to Jackson 3, and later removal of Jackson 2. The first step proposed is one PR with the shim types and one migrated parser package; no PR is referenced yet.

why_it_matters: Downstream users of iceberg-core's Jackson-typed APIs, including REST catalog servers, should expect those APIs to be deprecated in favour of Iceberg-owned types.
